sections.transcript: You've probably heard the theory. Firstborn children are reliable, middle children are sociable, lastborns crave the spotlight, and onlys are lonely. These notions, some would say stereotypes, arise from decades of research and form the backbone of hundreds of self-help and parenting books. The only problem? The notion that birth order affects personality is increasingly regarded by scientists as pure nonsense. One such expert is Dr. William Traeger of McGill University. He points to two recent international studies that turned up zero correlation between birth order and personality trait development. Traeger says past studies that posited a link between birth order and personality were fatally flawed. One blunder, says Traeger, was that researchers confounded their subject's birth order with their chronological age at the time of the study. For example, suppose an eldest child, 16-year-old Frank, was subjectively described by family members as reliable compared to his youngest sibling, 10-year-old Timmy. Research has concluded that Frank's reliability arose from the fact that he was first born. However, had the researchers come back six years later and repeated the questionnaire, Traeger says they probably would have found that Timmy, by then 16 years old himself, would be rated as equally reliable, despite being the youngest. For Traeger, continued belief in these theories theories is an indication of people's desires trumping their ability to reason. Despite these findings, Kirsten Grenville, CEO of Global Publishing, says books on birth order theory have propelled a raft of popular psychologists and parenting experts to the top of the best-seller charts. For Grenville, the issue isn't whether or not birth order theory is scientifically valid. The issue, rather, is whether or not it sells product and sell it does. Consumers seemingly insatiable appetite for these books, says Grenville, stems from the fact that almost everyone has an instinctive sense that birth order theories are true, whether or not they really are. People read these descriptions of sibling relationship dynamics and they think, yeah, that is true for me. Maybe the descriptions are like horoscopes. General enough that almost everyone can find something to agree with. Also, even if birth order doesn't scientifically correlate with personality trait development, there are certainly enough personal anecdotes, feelings, and hunches to suggest otherwise. So can we finally put to rest this notion that birth order matters from a scientific perspective? Dr. Traeger's response would be a qualified no. While personality may not be affected, birth order does appear to impact intelligence. Dr. Traeger says studies have proven that compared to their siblings, first-borns are smarter on average by a full IQ point.

paragraphs: Dear Ara,

Thank you for submitting your insurance claim to our office. I have finished reviewing it, including your photos of the water-damaged items and the original purchase receipts for them. I appreciated the itemized spreadsheet you included.

You have claimed the cost of replacing your desktop computer, which was for personal use only and damaged in the flood. The computer cannot be repaired, so the cost of replacing it is approved. However, your spreadsheet also itemizes the cost of a 3-year extended warranty, purchased along with the computer. Since the computer is 7 years old, the warranty coverage has expired. We cannot pay for the expired warranty portion of your computer costs.

You have also claimed the cost of the goods and services tax (GST) on the original purchase price of items that were damaged. Unfortunately, we pay this cost only on items that have been purchased as replacements. Therefore, for any replacement item you purchase, please submit the receipt to us. Note that interest on credit card purchases is not covered.

Regarding the wool carpet samples, you indicated that these are the property of the flooring company you work for. Our policy covers only property owned and used by you personally, so, I'm sorry, but we cannot cover the cost of the damaged carpet samples.

When it's time for you to renew your policy with us next spring, we recommend that you purchase additional insurance for items stored in your home but owned by or used in your business. This would protect you not only against the type of loss you recently experienced, but also against other risks such as fire.

Your adjusted total is $16,400. Our accounting department will issue you a cheque on the 15th of this month. If you would prefer to pick it up rather than receive it by mail, please let me know by this Wednesday at the latest.

As a valued long-time client, please accept warmest wishes from our family of companies. We wish you every success in recovering from your losses this past August, and we are pleased to have been able to assist you.
Regards,
Nelson Lowe

paragraphs: A. Photographs of spectacular rainbows are a dime a dozen, but a similar event seldom witnessed is the occurrence of moonbows. While rainbows are caused by beams of sunlight refracting through water droplets in the atmosphere, moonbows, as their name suggests, are created by beams of moonlight refracting through moisture in the air. However, this is where the similarity to rainbows ends. These nighttime bows, also referred to as lunar rainbows, are a much rarer phenomenon, occurring only at particular times of the year and limited by geographic requirements.

B. A distinct combination of astronomical and meteorological conditions is required in order for a moonbow to occur. For one, the moon must be bright, such as during a full or nearly full moon. Moreover, the moon must be low in the sky, no more than 42 degrees above the horizon. The lower the elevation of the moon, the fuller the lunar rainbow. Finally, there must be water droplets present in the atmosphere. The optimal conditions occur on nights during which there are rain showers falling opposite the moon and the sky is clear. Mist from waterfalls can also create the appropriate amount of moisture in the atmosphere. Under these precise conditions, a viewer standing with his or her back to the moon could potentially observe a moonbow.

C. Although multicoloured, the bands of the are of a moonbow appear as various shades of grey to the naked eye. This can be attributed to physiological factors. Because it is difficult for the human eye to discern colours at low levels of illumination, such as in the darkness of night, the multihued bow appears white or grey. Nonetheless, the magnificent colours of lunar bows can be picked up in long-exposure photographs, even though the are appears monochrome to the photographer.

D. Because of the specific combination of conditions required, moonbows are more prevalent in certain locations around the world, particularly those that have waterfalls. Such moonbows form fairly regularly at Yosemite Falls in California, Cumberland Falls in Kentucky, and Victoria Falls on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe in Africa. In fact, moonbow predictions at some of these locations can be found on various websites. The appearance of lunar rainbows is also common in the cloud forests of Costa Rica and in certain areas of Hawaii. If you are fortunate enough to be at the right place at the right time, you may be able to catch a glimpse of this magnificent phenomenon.
E. Not given in any of the above paragraphs.

left.intro: Read the following article from a website.
paragraphs: Smartphones and other technological paraphernalia have invaded our lives. We are now surrounded by people eschewing social etiquette by compulsively checking their phones, drawn automatically to the incessant "ding" of their notifications. The ubiquity and nature of this modern technology have made concentrating on anything for more than a moment feel like a Herculean task. Young children are particularly at risk, since their neurological development is not yet complete.

The impression that children are negatively affected by personal computing devices is reflected in anecdotal evidence from classrooms, where teachers increasingly report shortened attention spans in pupils. Lisa Cranberg, a veteran elementary school teacher, believes that "exposure to technology is rewiring our kids' brains." For her, "children spending extended periods of time interacting solely with their smartphones is showing diminished self-awareness, emotional intelligence, and focus." In essence, she believes that overstimulation is making it difficult for students to concentrate in a traditional lecture-centric classroom.

Not everyone is as anxious, however, about technological advances. Dr. Clara Hughes of the University of Waterloo agrees that shifts in stimuli are resulting in cerebral rewiring, with ramifications that might include shorter attention spans. However, she claims that developing these mechanisms that allow us to partake in rapid-fire attention shifting is actually "beneficial to creative types whose job is to amalgamate disparate ideas." She surmises that our brains are simply adapting to the level of stimulation inherent to our environment.

In fact, while technology can be harmful to concentration, a new wave of research is unearthing a whole slew of unforeseen beneficial effects. "Modern technology is bettering our ability to multitask and concentrate in short bursts," according to neuropsychologist Dr. Mark Levinson. This means that "we get a better sense of what deserves our attention, and there is an improved selection of the information we commit to memory."

Dr. Hughes is more moderate in her analysis, saying that "overexposure and gadget addiction do have a demonstrably negative effect on many cognitive behaviours." Nevertheless, she concurs with Dr. Levinson's overall beneficial assessment of the neurological side-effects of our interactions with digital technologies.

tasks.title: Responding to Survey Questions
scenario: Your apartment manager is surveying your opinion about the swimming pool in your building. Currently, your building has a swimming pool, but it is really old and needs to be renovated. Some tenants prefer to have a small gym instead of a pool. The apartment manager has asked you to complete an opinion survey.
tasks.instruction: Choose the option that you prefer. Why do you prefer your choice? Explain the reasons for your choice. Write about 150-200 words.
options: Option A: I would like to keep the swimming pool.
Option B: I would like to have a gym.

paragraphs: To: Manager

For me, I would prefer to have the gym instead of swimming pool cause especially during winter time a pool is not useful. The gym is better cause every of us needs some exercise when done in work and most of all it can be relaxing for the health of the tenants. I love biking in the gym and use lots apparatus of the gym. And I make leisure time of myself its because whole weekend I'm busy of work. The good thing is it lesser the time than we go in other fitness center. I'm hoping lots of tenants wants the gym instead of swimming pool. I know there's a lot of lovers of fitness especially the weather is so cold. And later we you can build a good relationship to your tenant. Make sure that what your tenants want you must support the opinion.
Hi,

So here are my reasons for keeping the swimming pool. First of all, I use this pool every day, along with a number of other residents. We also have parties here and swimming lesions for the young children in the building. I think that swimming is a better way to get exercise, as it is easier on your joints and bones because it is a low impact activity. We also have water aerobics every morning and evening for all ages. The pool just needs a little TLC but a gym would need to have a new space and new equipment and would be very costly. It would be very easy for someone that does not know what they are doing to get badly hurt in the gym on some of the heavy equipment. Another point about the swimming pool is that it's so great to help cool down in the summer. Also, there is a brand new gym only three blocks from here and they have great new starter deals that I think the residence might be very happy with. I hope this helps.
Filipe
Dear Apartment Manager,
Thank you for your invitation to complete a survey regarding the issue of the swimming pool in the building.

As a long-time resident of this building, I feel that the swimming pool is out dated and in much need of repair. In the time I have been a resident here, I have never used the pool facility and consider it to be unnecessary. It is my opinion that it would be far more beneficial to residents of the building if you were to consider installing a small gym instead of renovating the swimming pool.

After speaking with a number of my neighbours, it seems that many would favour the gym instead of the swimming pool particularly due to the cold weather in Calgary often making the idea of swimming unappealing. I know that a number of residents would prefer to have gym here in the building so it would enable them to exercise at various times of the day and also cut down on the additional expense of an outside gym membership.
I would like to thank you for your time and hope that you will consider my opinion when making your decision.
Regards,
Elizabeth
